stem.text: A potential divider circuit is formed by connecting a battery of negligible internal resistance in series with two variable resistors, as shown.

stem.alt: Circuit diagram of a battery connected in a loop with two variable resistors in series, labelled RX and RY, with a double-headed arrow labelled VX across the resistor RX.

stem.text: The variable resistors have resistances $R_\text{X}$ and $R_\text{Y}$.
$V_\text{X}$ is the potential difference (p.d.) across the variable resistor with resistance $R_\text{X}$.
$R_\text{X}$ and $R_\text{Y}$ are both changed at the same time.
Which combination of changes **must** cause $V_\text{X}$ to increase?
